successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the eastern remnant in northern Côte d'Ivoire at the capture of Samori

ledger.x: 1878: Samori Ture declares himself faama at Bissandugu.
c. 1878: Kouroussa submits. "Kouroussa, Norassoba, Baro: taken with Baté allies after 1875; no exact years given."
by 1878: Samori holds the Buré gold fields.
1879: Samori besieges Kankan and installs a puppet ruler.
July 1884: a council makes Islam the state religion and Samori takes the title Almamy.
1885: Colonel Combes's column tries to seize the Buré gold fields by taking Niagassola; Samory counterattacks and the French withdraw.
28 March 1886: the Treaty of Kéniéba Koura ends the first war.
April 1887: Samori besieges Sikasso, capital of Kénédougou.
1888: Samori gives up the siege of Sikasso by the end of the rainy season; "The French took Sikasso on May 1, 1898."
10 March 1891: Colonel Archinard attacks from Nyamina and opens the second war.
11 April 1891: the French take Kankan and find Bissandougou deserted.
January 1892: Colonel Humbert attacks Bissandougou; the city is abandoned again, so the home country is lost.
9 May 1892: at Frankonedou Samori decides to move the empire east to Kabadougou.
early 1893: the French take Faranah, cut the arms routes and the western vassals surrender; Kouroussa, Buré and Wassoulou pass to the French.
1893: the western war ends with the surrender of the vassals; Samori fights on in the east.
February 1895: Samori moves his base to Dabakala.
April 1895: Kong pledges loyalty to Samori after the French retreat of 14 March.
December 1896: Samori's son Saranken Mori takes Bouna.
23 May 1897: Samori destroys Kong after a revolt.
23 May 1897: Samori destroys Kong and the Kong country passes from vassalage to direct Samorian hold.
29 September 1898: Samori is captured at Guelemou and the empire ends.

wars.name: First Franco-Samorian war (First Mandingo War)
wars.outcome: Kiniéran sacked 21 February 1882, Samaya 26 February; French fort at Bamako 1 February 1883; Combes withdrew from Niagassola 1885; the Treaty of Kéniéba Koura (28 March 1886) gave France the Niger left bank up to Siguiri and left Samori Buré and the Manding.

wars.name: Siege of Sikasso
wars.outcome: Samori besieged Sikasso for about 15 months from April 1887 and abandoned the siege by the end of the 1888 rainy season; it did not fall to him.

wars.name: Second Franco-Samorian war
wars.outcome: Kankan fell 11 April 1891, Bissandougou was abandoned January 1892, Faranah fell early 1893 and the western vassals surrendered; Samori rebased in Kabadougou (9 May 1892).

wars.name: Third Franco-Samorian war
wars.outcome: Captain Braulot was killed outside Bouna on 20 August 1897; the French took Sikasso on 1 May 1898 and Gouraud captured Samori at Guelemou on 29 September 1898.

certainty.note: No treaty line was ever surveyed; the 1886 treaty fixes only the Niger up to Siguiri as the western limit, and the eastern empire after 1892 was a moving camp.
